A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SIPDO and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite substantial reformatting: v1 Appendices A–E largely correspond to v3 Appendices B–F.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original benchmark evaluations across several LLMs, difficulty-gradient ablations, and qualitative experiments. The appendices provide optimized prompts and generated examples.

after.justification: V3 retains the original evaluations and adds MMLU results, difficulty and resource-cost measurements, and voter and component ablations in Table 1 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: V3 adds unanimous validation by three expert agents before difficult/MMLU synthetic examples reach the prompt optimizer (Sections 3.3 and 4.2). This is an additional procedural component, distinct from v1's rule-based reflection check. The generator, progressive curriculum, and local/global prompt-refinement loop remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 retains BIG-Bench, ProofWriter, FOLIO, and PrOntoQA and adds MMLU College Biology, College Computer Science, and Machine Learning. These evaluations substantially extend coverage to expert factual knowledge and subject-specific problem solving.

E2.justification: V3 Table 1 introduces evaluated comparisons with TextGrad across all three MMLU subjects, Momentum-Enhanced TextGrad on Computer Science and Machine Learning, and ANN on Machine Learning. REVOLVE also participates but was already evaluated in v1. Comparator membership in the retained BIG-Bench and logical-reasoning tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated Penguins and Geometric Shapes difficulty/iteration budget changes from 20 to 25. New experiments sweep difficulty levels 5, 10, 15, and 20, measure time, money, and tokens, and introduce component-removal controls. MMLU uses a newly described GPT-4o optimization/GPT-4o-mini testing configuration. Unchanged original benchmark scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun under the revised budget.

E4.justification: V3 Appendix A adds difficulty–cost sensitivity, runtime comparisons with PromptAgent, voter removal, and removal of the generator, error-analysis component, and revisor. Figure 2 and Table 17 add an estimated complexity analysis and examples across difficulty levels. The original no-gradient and one-shot-extremes analyses remain, while the separate rule-based reflection-check analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3 Figure 2 introduces an 'Estimated range' between minimum and maximum reasoning turns, but provides no estimation or sampling procedure. It is unclear whether this represents uncertainty reporting or only an illustrative difficulty range.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and no-gradient accuracy values are retained in v3 Tables 2–4. New results include SIPDO's MMLU scores of 93.0% for Computer Science, 93.8% for Machine Learning, and 96.5% for Biology, with the latter tying TextGrad and REVOLVE. Tables 5–8 add extensive cost and ablation outcomes. V3 also adds comparison margins; Table 3's GPT-4o average margin of 4.2 conflicts with its displayed 86.4 and 82.0 scores.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, worst-case bound, and four-step proof are substantively unchanged; v1 Appendix E matches v3 Appendix F. V3 corrects the theorem's assumption references to A1–A5 and expands practical discussion of label validation, but adds no mathematical argument or revised guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same principal claims: synthetic-data feedback enables iterative prompt improvement, exposes weaknesses, and improves reasoning/QA performance without additional external supervision. The expanded introduction, rewritten conclusion, and additional benchmarks do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies the smaller-model difficulty-gradient interpretation to the OpenAI model family and explicitly discusses unexpected synthetic labels as motivation for voter filtering. V1's explicit latency/cost limitation and rationale for disabling the reflection check disappear. The need for evaluation on financial or clinical corpora remains in the conclusion.

D1.justification: V3 Section 4.2 and Appendix D provide operational generation, error-analysis, recommendation, and refinement templates, substantially extending v1's illustrative outputs. V3 newly discloses temperatures of 0.5 for generation, 0.7 for recommendations, and 0.0 for analysis/refinement and testing, alongside validation and resource-use information. V1's real-data, accuracy-threshold refinement description is omitted without explaining whether that procedure changed.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands its treatment of existing feedback-loop approaches, adding Self-Refine, Promptbreeder, recursive in-context prompt generation, SPO, DLPO, and CriSPO. MMLU, TextGrad, and ANN references accompany the expanded evaluation. The Least-to-Most discussion and citation are removed; merging duplicate references to the same Gao work is only bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: V3 extensively expands the introduction, subdivides related work, and reorganizes the experimental narrative into separate setup, implementation, results, and ablation sections. The conclusion is rewritten, the standalone Limitations section is removed, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, substantially reflowing equations, tables, and prose. V3 adds the MMLU table, four Appendix A tables, Figure 2, and the difficulty-indexed example table. Prompt documentation gains styled template panels. The original workflow diagram and benchmark tables remain, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V3 improves reproducibility through operational templates and disclosed settings, while component, voter, and cost ablations make important tradeoffs easier to assess than in v1. These gains support a limited overall improvement. However, new reporting problems constrain confidence: Table 1 labels MMLU results as GPT-4o while Section 4.3 specifies GPT-4o-mini testing, and Table 16 adds an incorrect answer of four for six listed musical instruments. The expanded evidence therefore does not establish a major quality improvement.
